title: No third trombone part: composing his own
summary: There were no third trombone parts, so he composed his own and played first trombone with the trumpet lead.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So how long had you been playing with Duke on May 16th, when you recorded with him for the first time? How long did it take to get across the country?

Well, what happened there was, now there were no third trombone parts. So I had to sort of compose my own parts, and mostly I played -- all the time I played first trombone, which is most compatible to first trumpet, you had the lead. So it would be a double lead, you know, trombone and trumpet, or something, whatever it was. And I did all that myself. Until they finally got some skeletons together, arrangements.
And then as the new numbers came out, they started arranging for the third trombone or the third man, we'll say. But up to that time, there were no third parts written.
Did it surprise you to join a band and find that there was no part for you?

Not too much, because that -- all bands at that time, or most of the bands, were mostly ear bands. You -- whatever you heard you'd pick up a place to fit in, or a part to fit in. You'd either place first, second or third, or once in a while fourth notes stuck in the triads, and then became the fourth notes would be injected.
So you just went along, and whatever you heard was missing, that's where you were.
